note: Unbaked. Dialogue lines in scene order, then the MAKE HIM LAUGH battle lines (kind praise, keyed by speaker id). The porch Deedee and armored Boppy use the existing Deedee and Boppy voices.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. It’s Tom. I’m right in front of you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Halt.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He said that before. He’s going to say it again. He’s going to say it until we do something about it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tom. Behind us, down the stairs, something is coming up the tunnel. A lot of clipboards. I counted fourteen.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara growls, low. She has opinions about clipboards.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Sol’s handcar is right behind them with the girls. I’ll send them up. Nara and I will hold the breach. Somebody has to be at the bottom of the stairs to say no.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re staying in a tunnel full of Auditors.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I used to carry coffee through a film set at five in the morning. I can handle an Auditor.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Take the thermos. They hate a thermos.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I never leave without it. Go fix the door, Tom. I’ll fix the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Be careful. Please. I mean that in a very specific, very annoying way.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I know. I’ll be careful in the exact way you’re being annoying about right now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: MOMMY. We took a handcar. It has a HORN.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I honked it at the tunnel and the tunnel honked BACK. I said it was rude. It said honk.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol was supposed to keep you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Sol said, and I quote, “I’m not stopping them. I’ve met them.”

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is Boppy a statue? Can I climb him?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Rose. Grace. Go back to the cab.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, you have a bucket on your head.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It’s a helm.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s a bucket.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Why is Boppy a knight? Is this a quest? Is there a quest log? Do I get a badge?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Girls. Stay behind me. He’s not himself.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He’s completely himself. That’s the problem. He’s himself with a gate.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So. Where’s Deedee?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Inside. She’s fine. She’s making a crisp. Don’t look at the porch.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy. There’s a Deedee on the porch.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That’s a decoration.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: She waved.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. First the porch. Then Dad. Nobody touches the armor. Not even a little. Rose, that includes you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I wasn’t going to touch it. I was going to boop it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Rose.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A very small boop.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Rhubarb crisp, nine minutes. Rhubarb crisp, nine minutes. Hello, sweetie. Rhubarb crisp, nine minutes.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. It’s Amy. Mom, look at me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hello, Amy. Rhubarb crisp, nine minutes. Do you want a bite? Rhubarb crisp. Nine minutes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s looping. Look at the tray. It’s the same crisp. Every time. It’s fresh, it’s perfect, and nobody ever eats it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amber is warmth that got stuck. She’s been giving it to nobody for hours. It needs somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Maybe nobody ate it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. That is the smartest thing you have said all week.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I say smart things every day. They just come out as noise.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee. I’m going to eat the crisp now. Okay? Okay.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ...It’s SO good. It’s the best one. Deedee, it’s the best one you ever made.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. Somebody ate it. Oh, Rosie.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh. I was making that for a long time, wasn’t I.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Amy. Tommy. My girls. How long was I gone?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A while.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your father put on that armor. He said the glass would keep us all safe. He’s been standing out there for hours and he hasn’t sat down. Not once. Not for his back.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: He thinks the armor takes the ache away. It doesn’t. It just stops him from feeling it. There’s a difference. I was a nurse for forty years. There is a very big difference.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Can you walk?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The glass has my feet. It’s up to my knees. I can’t go anywhere. But I can see him.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Don’t hit him, Tommy. He can’t be hit. He hates being hit and it makes the gold stronger. Make him laugh. He laughs when he’s scared. He did at our wedding.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I have a whole bit.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I have a whole VIDEO.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad used to run cross country. If I can get him to walk a lap, I can get him to talk.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: When he’s ready, I’ll call out. You won’t miss it. I’ve been calling that man for fifty years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be careful.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You were always the careful one. Now be the kind one. Go.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. We’re not here to fight you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then you’re here to leave.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom’s on the porch. She’s awake.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: She is NOT. She’s fine. She’s baking. That’s the deal. Nobody gets hurt, nobody gets old, nobody gets left.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Stand down, Tommy. I don’t want to hurt you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then don’t. And I won’t hurt you either.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The gold hums. It likes it when somebody swings. I can’t stop it from liking it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: So we just don’t swing!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We’re the opposite of swinging. We’re the family that shows up.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Last warning.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Noted.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Walk it off. He hits like a dad who loves you and is very upset about it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The gold goes soft. Then it runs, slow, down the front of him, like warm wax, and soaks into the porch. The helmet is the last to go.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The bucket rolled down the steps. Can I have it? Is it mine?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Ow.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Ow. My back. My back is back.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The ache came back!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: It never left. I just had a bucket on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A man in a long coat came to the door. Very polite. He never took his hat off. He said he could stop the aches. Stop the slowing down.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He said the girls would be safe. In the good part, forever. All I had to do was stand here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And you said yes.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I signed a thing. It said WARDEN on the top. I didn’t read the bottom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody reads the bottom.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I’m seventy-some years old. Every year the girls get faster and I get slower. I’m not mad about it. I’m just... one day I won’t be able to catch you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I just didn’t want to get too old to keep you all safe.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You big nut.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: We keep each other safe. That is the whole deal. That’s the only one. You don’t get to keep us safe alone.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Deedee.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Robert.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is this the part where everybody cries?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Yes. Rose. Yes it is.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy. You’re allowed to be slow. We’ll wait. I’ll film it. For the memories. I’ll pause and wait for you.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’ll walk slow. I’ll walk like a snail. A snail wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Rosie. That’s the best offer I’ve had in eleven years.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Dad. Come on. I’ll walk you in. Short laps. You can complain the whole time.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My stomach is doing something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: There he is.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance said the girls would be safe in the good part, forever. We told him no once. He won’t take it well.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Take the key, Tommy. It opens the gate. It also opens the door. It doesn’t matter which. Nobody gets past us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets past us.

battleLines.speaker: tom
battleLines.text: Dad. You have been standing here so long the pigeons named you. Gary. They call you Gary.

battleLines.speaker: tom
battleLines.text: Dad, I said I would never hit you and then I stood next to you and now I realize that’s the same thing as a very large lawn ornament.

battleLines.speaker: grace
battleLines.text: Knock knock! Who’s there? Boppy! Boppy who? Boppy, take off the bucket, it’s not Halloween!

battleLines.speaker: grace
battleLines.text: Why did Boppy cross the road? To complain about the other side! I did a whole video on it and it has seven likes. They’re all mine.

battleLines.speaker: rose
battleLines.text: Boppy, is your hat a BUCKET? Can I wear it? Can I wear the bucket? Knock knock! Bucket!

battleLines.speaker: rose
battleLines.text: Is it a bath? Are you in a metal bath? Boppy, I want to be in a metal bath!

battleLines.speaker: amy
battleLines.text: Dad. Elbows down. Stride out. You haven’t walked at a proper clip in eleven years. Come on. Pick up your feet.

battleLines.speaker: amy
battleLines.text: You’ve been standing for hours. I’ll walk with you. Short laps. You can complain the entire time.
